objects.description: Reference-counted wrapper for an arbitrary user-provided data pointer. The data field points to the payload; ref points to an internal reference-counting owner (Dav1dRef) that tracks the allocation origin. The exact lifecycle semantics of Dav1dRef are not defined in this header; consumers should treat ref as an opaque handle and avoid modifying it directly.

Metadata associated with an input data packet, propagated to the decoded output image. Fields include timestamp, duration, byte offset, packet size, and a user-configurable user_data block. Intended to carry container/stream information through the decoder unchanged; exact defaults and interpretation are noted in comments.

Parameter block describing picture geometry and format for allocation/processing: width, height, pixel layout (enum Dav1dPixelLayout, defined elsewhere), and bits per component (8 or 10). Used to size and allocate picture buffers.

Primary image container for decoded AV1 frames: holds planar YUV data pointers and strides, picture parameters, metadata pointers, reference-counting handles, and allocator private data. Buffers are typically provided via Dav1dPicAllocator. Fields like seq_hdr, frame_hdr, and metadata pointers point to separately managed objects.

objects.definition:
typedef struct Dav1dPicAllocator {
    void *cookie; ///< custom data to pass to the allocator callbacks.
    /**
     * Allocate the picture buffer based on the Dav1dPictureParameters.
     *
     * The data[0], data[1] and data[2] must be DAV1D_PICTURE_ALIGNMENT byte
     * aligned and with a pixel width/height multiple of 128 pixels. Any
     * allocated memory area should also be padded by DAV1D_PICTURE_ALIGNMENT
     * bytes.
     * data[1] and data[2] must share the same stride[1].
     *
     * This function will be called on the main thread (the thread which calls
     * dav1d_get_picture()).
     *
     * @param  pic The picture to allocate the buffer for. The callback needs to
     *             fill the picture data[0], data[1], data[2], stride[0] and
     *             stride[1].
     *             The allocator can fill the pic allocator_data pointer with
     *             a custom pointer that will be passed to
     *             release_picture_callback().
     * @param cookie Custom pointer passed to all calls.
     *
     * @note No fields other than data, stride and allocator_data must be filled
     *       by this callback.
     * @return 0 on success. A negative DAV1D_ERR value on error.
     */
    int (*alloc_picture_callback)(Dav1dPicture *pic, void *cookie);
    /**
     * Release the picture buffer.
     *
     * If frame threading is used, this function may be called by the main
     * thread (the thread which calls dav1d_get_picture()) or any of the frame
     * threads and thus must be thread-safe. If frame threading is not used,
     * this function will only be called on the main thread.
     *
     * @param pic    The picture that was filled by alloc_picture_callback().
     * @param cookie Custom pointer passed to all calls.
     */
    void (*release_picture_callback)(Dav1dPicture *pic, void *cookie);
} Dav1dPicAllocator;
objects.description: User-supplied allocator vtable for picture buffer management. Provides a cookie and two callbacks: one to allocate and fill Dav1dPicture data/strides with proper alignment and padding, and one to release them. Thread-safety requirements apply to the release callback when frame threading is used.

objects.definition: struct Dav1dRef;
objects.description: Opaque reference-counted handle used internally to track allocation origin and lifetime of headers, metadata, and frame buffers. Only a forward declaration is present here; definition is elsewhere.

Opaque-like data holder for an encoded bitstream buffer and its associated metadata. It stores a pointer to immutable bytes, their size, a reference-counted allocation origin (Dav1dRef, defined elsewhere), and user-provided metadata (Dav1dDataProps, defined in common.h). Used as the input container to dav1d APIs for wrapping/allocating/freeing input data.
OBU (Open Bitstream Unit) types as defined by AV1. Used to identify the kind of OBU encountered in the bitstream.
Transform mode signaling permitted in a frame (e.g., only 4x4, largest allowed, or fully switchable).
Interpolation filter selection for subpel motion: specific 8-tap variants, bilinear, or switchable.
Tri-state boolean used in sequence header signaling: off, on, or adaptively selected by the encoder/bitstream.
In-loop restoration filter type per plane: none, switchable, Wiener, or self-guided restoration (SGRPROJ).
Global/warped motion model type: identity, translation, rotation+zoom, or full affine.
Holds a warped/global motion model: the model type, 3x2 fixed-point matrix parameters, and unpacked alpha/beta/gamma/delta coefficients.
Pixel format layout (monochrome or YUV 4:2:0 / 4:2:2 / 4:4:4).
AV1 frame coding type: key, inter, intra (non-key), or switch. Used in frame headers.

objects.definition: typedef struct Dav1dContext Dav1dContext;
objects.description: Opaque decoder context type for a dav1d decoder instance. Only forward-declared here; created with dav1d_open() and freed with dav1d_close().

objects.definition: typedef struct Dav1dRef Dav1dRef;
objects.description: Opaque internal reference-counted buffer handle. Only forward-declared here; definition not provided in this header.
Configurable logger with a user cookie and a vprintf-style callback used by the library for diagnostics. Set in Dav1dSettings to enable logging.
Bitmask flags selecting which AV1 in-loop filters to apply: deblocking, CDEF, and restoration. Used within Dav1dSettings.
Selector for which frame types to decode and return (all, reference-only, intra-only, key-only). Used in Dav1dSettings.

Configuration parameters for a dav1d decoder instance, including threading, buffering, film grain, SVC operating point, frame size limits, allocators, logging, compliance, output behavior, and in-loop filtering. Initialize with dav1d_default_settings() before use.
Bitmask flags signaling decoder events associated with recently returned pictures (e.g., new sequence header or new operating parameters info). Used with dav1d_get_event_flags().

functions.name: dav1d_data_props_unref
functions.description: Releases the reference(s) held by a Dav1dDataProps instance, typically unreferencing any associated user_data/ref internals so that resources can be reclaimed. Use when you are done with the metadata copied from an input packet. After this call, any internal references the structure held may be invalid, so treat the contents as no longer owning referenced resources unless reinitialized. Exact side-effects beyond releasing references are not documented in this header.
requirements: props must be a valid, non-null pointer to a Dav1dDataProps.
props must be initialized by the caller such that its internal references (e.g., user_data.ref) are either NULL or valid references created/managed by the dav1d API.
Do not reuse any released internal pointers/references from props after this call unless you have reinitialized them.
The function does not return an error; callers should not expect a return value or errno to be set.

functions.name: dav1d_picture_unref
functions.description: Release a reference to a Dav1dPicture. Typically used by callers after they are done consuming a decoded frame to drop their reference and allow underlying buffers to be freed via the allocator when the last reference is gone. After this call, the picture should be considered uninitialized/empty and its fields must not be accessed unless it is reinitialized by the decoder or allocator. Note: The header only states that it releases a reference; detailed refcounting and side effects are not documented here and are inferred from typical dav1d API behavior.
requirements: p must point to a Dav1dPicture that currently holds a valid reference (inferred from function name and typical ref/unref patterns).
Do not access fields of *p after calling this function unless it has been reinitialized or repopulated by the library (inferred).
Thread-safety, allowance of NULL, and idempotency (calling multiple times) are not documented here; behavior for those cases is unknown.

functions.name: dav1d_data_create
functions.description: Allocate an internal buffer of size sz for a Dav1dData and associate it with the provided data context. On success, returns a pointer to the allocated buffer; on failure, returns NULL. Typical usage is to prepare a Dav1dData to hold sz bytes of input bitstream before passing it to the decoder.
requirements: data must be a valid pointer to a Dav1dData structure (input/output parameter).
sz specifies the size, in bytes, of the buffer to allocate; allowable range is unknown from this header.
Caller must check the return value: non-NULL indicates success; NULL indicates allocation failure.
Error handling strategy beyond returning NULL is not specified in this header.

functions.name: dav1d_data_wrap
functions.signature: int dav1d_data_wrap(Dav1dData *data, const uint8_t *buf, size_t sz, void (*free_callback)(const uint8_t *buf, void *cookie), void *cookie);
functions.description: Wrap an existing data buffer buf of size sz into a Dav1dData without copying. When the last reference to the wrapped data is released, free_callback is invoked with the original buf and cookie so the caller can free or otherwise finalize the memory. Returns 0 on success or a negative DAV1D_ERR code on error.
requirements: data must be a valid pointer to a Dav1dData structure to receive the wrapped buffer.
buf must point to an existing data array of at least sz bytes; ownership remains with the wrapper until the last reference is released.
free_callback will be called exactly when the last reference to this wrapped data is released; it receives the same buf and cookie passed here.
cookie is an opaque pointer value passed through to free_callback; its content/lifetime must remain valid until free_callback is called.
Thread-safety requirements for free_callback are not specified for this function in this header (unknown).
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; a negative DAV1D_ERR value indicates failure.
Behavior and allowance of NULL free_callback are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: dav1d_data_wrap_user_data
functions.signature: int dav1d_data_wrap_user_data(Dav1dData *data, const uint8_t *user_data, void (*free_callback)(const uint8_t *user_data, void *cookie), void *cookie);
functions.description: Wrap a user-provided pointer user_data into a reference-counted object stored in data->m.user_data. When the last reference is released, free_callback is invoked on the same thread that released it (if frame threading is used, make sure it is thread-safe). Returns 0 on success or a negative DAV1D_ERR on error.
requirements: data must be a valid pointer to a Dav1dData structure.
user_data is an opaque user pointer to be wrapped; its interpretation is up to the caller.
free_callback will be called when the last reference is released, with user_data and cookie as provided.
free_callback will be invoked on the same thread that releases the last reference; if frame threading is used, free_callback must be thread-safe.
cookie is an opaque pointer passed to free_callback and must remain valid until free_callback is called.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; a negative DAV1D_ERR value indicates failure.
Whether user_data or free_callback may be NULL is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: dav1d_data_unref
functions.description: Release a Dav1dData reference. Decrements the reference count for data->m.user_data if it was initialized via dav1d_data_wrap_user_data, and then memset the Dav1dData object to zero.
requirements: data must be a valid pointer to a Dav1dData structure; it will be zeroed after the call.

If data->m.user_data was initialized with dav1d_data_wrap_user_data, its reference count will be decremented; any associated free callbacks may be invoked accordingly (timing specifics beyond this are not detailed here).
Function returns no status; callers should not use the contents of data after calling, as it is zeroed.

functions.name: dav1d_version
functions.description: Return the library version string. Use to display or log the linked dav1d version.

functions.name: dav1d_version_api
functions.description: Return the library API version as 0x00XXYYZZ (XX=major, YY=minor, ZZ=patch). Useful for compile- or run-time compatibility checks.

functions.name: dav1d_default_settings
functions.description: Initialize a Dav1dSettings struct to safe default values. Call before customizing settings used to open a decoder.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL pointer to writable Dav1dSettings storage.

functions.name: dav1d_open
functions.description: Allocate and open a decoder instance using the provided settings. On success, *c_out receives the created decoder. The decoder must later be closed with dav1d_close.
requirements: c_out must be non-NULL and point to a location where the created Dav1dContext* can be stored.
s must point to a valid Dav1dSettings (e.g., set via dav1d_default_settings) or be configured according to the struct’s documented fields.
On success, the caller must eventually call dav1d_close(&ctx) to free resources.
Return value must be checked: 0 indicates success; negative values are DAV1D_ERR codes.

functions.name: dav1d_parse_sequence_header
functions.signature: int dav1d_parse_sequence_header(Dav1dSequenceHeader *out, const uint8_t *buf, const size_t sz);
functions.description: Parse a Sequence Header OBU from the provided buffer. Safe to pass buffers containing other OBU types; only the last Sequence Header, if any, is returned in out.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to writable Dav1dSequenceHeader storage.
buf must be a valid pointer to at least sz bytes of readable memory (may contain zero or more OBUs).
sz is the size in bytes of buf.
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; DAV1D_ERR(ENOENT) if no Sequence Header present; other negative DAV1D_ERR for invalid data/args.

functions.name: dav1d_send_data
functions.description: Feed one or more AV1 OBUs to the decoder. On success, ownership of the Dav1dData reference is transferred to the library. If the decoder cannot accept more input (EAGAIN), obtain frames via dav1d_get_picture and retry.
requirements: c must be a valid, opened Dav1dContext.
in must be a valid pointer to a Dav1dData containing input data; on success, ownership is transferred to the decoder and the caller must not reuse it.
If the function returns DAV1D_ERR(EAGAIN), the caller should call dav1d_get_picture() to retrieve frames before retrying.
If a negative error other than EAGAIN is returned, the input reference remains owned by the caller and must be managed by the caller.
Return value must be checked for success (0) or negative DAV1D_ERR codes.

functions.name: dav1d_get_picture
functions.description: Return a decoded picture if available. On success, the caller assumes ownership of the returned picture reference. Use repeatedly to drain frames (e.g., at end of stream until EAGAIN).
requirements: c must be a valid, opened Dav1dContext.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to writable Dav1dPicture storage.
Caller must check return value: 0 on success (one frame returned); DAV1D_ERR(EAGAIN) if more input is needed; other negative DAV1D_ERR for errors.
On success, the caller assumes ownership of the picture reference and must unref/free it via the appropriate dav1d picture unref function or allocator semantics.

functions.name: dav1d_apply_grain
functions.description: Apply film grain synthesis to a previously decoded picture. If the source picture lacks grain metadata, a new reference is returned without modification. Note: if Dav1dSettings.apply_grain was enabled during decoding, calling this will apply grain a second time.
requirements: c must be a valid, opened Dav1dContext.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to writable Dav1dPicture storage; on success, caller takes ownership of the returned reference.
in must be a valid pointer to a previously decoded Dav1dPicture; no ownership is transferred.
Caller must check return value for success (0) or negative DAV1D_ERR codes.

functions.name: dav1d_close
functions.description: Close a decoder instance and free all associated resources. Sets *c_out to NULL.
requirements: c_out must be non-NULL and point to a Dav1dContext* previously returned by dav1d_open.
After return, *c_out is set to NULL and must no longer be used.

functions.name: dav1d_flush
functions.description: Flush delayed frames and clear the decoder’s internal state (used for seeking). Decoding resumes after a valid Sequence Header OBU is delivered via dav1d_send_data.
requirements: c must be a valid, opened Dav1dContext.
After flushing, the caller must provide a valid sequence header in subsequent input before decoding can start again.

functions.name: dav1d_get_event_flags
functions.description: Fetch a bitmask of decoding event flags (e.g., new sequence or new operating parameters) and clear them in the decoder.
requirements: c must be a valid, opened Dav1dContext.
flags must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for the bitmask.
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; negative DAV1D_ERR codes on error.
Note: calling this clears the stored event flags in the decoder.

functions.name: dav1d_get_decode_error_data_props
functions.description: Retrieve user-provided metadata (Dav1dDataProps) associated with the input packet that caused the last reported decoding error (a negative return from dav1d_send_data or dav1d_get_picture, excluding EAGAIN). On success, the caller assumes ownership of the returned reference.
requirements: c must be a valid, opened Dav1dContext.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to writable Dav1dDataProps storage.
Meaningful only after a decoding error has been reported to the user (negative return value other than EAGAIN from dav1d_send_data or dav1d_get_picture).
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; negative DAV1D_ERR codes on error.
On success, caller assumes ownership of the returned reference and must manage its lifetime appropriately.

functions.name: dav1d_get_frame_delay
functions.description: Return the decoder’s frame delay (number of internally buffered frames, excluding references) for a context configured with the provided settings; guaranteed to be >= 1 and <= max_frame_delay.
requirements: s must point to a valid Dav1dSettings instance representing the configuration used (or to be used) for the decoder.
Caller must check return value: non-negative delay on success; negative DAV1D_ERR code on error.
The returned delay is valid only for a Dav1dContext initialized with these settings.

endpoint_classifiers.name: dav1d_parse_sequence_header
data_types: AV1 bitstream (OBU sequence header or mixed OBUs)

data_types.description: An unrestricted sequence of bytes with no required encoding or structure. May contain any values (0x00–0xFF) and any length as provided by the fuzzer. Suitable for APIs that accept raw buffers without a specified format.

data_types.data_type: AV1 bitstream (OBU sequence header or mixed OBUs)
data_types.description: A buffer containing AV1 OBUs (Open Bitstream Units) as defined by the AV1 specification. The data may include a Sequence Header OBU and can be mixed with other OBU types; parsers typically scan the buffer and extract the last Sequence Header if present. Bytes must follow AV1 OBU syntax to be considered valid.

generators.generator:
import os
import random
from typing import List

# This generator targets dav1d_data_create / dav1d_data_wrap / dav1d_data_wrap_user_data
# fuzzer stubs. They copy a payload from FUZZ_PARAM_STR into allocated buffers.
# We therefore generate interesting arbitrary binary blobs sized within the harness
# bounds (up to 1024 for data buffers, up to 64 for user_data). We mix sizes and
# contents to exercise different paths while staying valid.

MAX_CREATE_WRAP = 1024  # matches stub upper bound
MAX_USER_DATA = 64      # matches stub upper bound
MAX_TOTAL = 4096        # overall cap

ASCII_MARKERS: List[bytes] = [
    b"\x00",                    # NUL presence
    b"\xff",                    # all-ones byte
    b"DAV1D",                   # library tag
    b"OBU\x00\x01\x02",        # AV1-like OBU marker fragment
    b"SEQHDR",                  # sequence header text
    b"FRAME",                   # frame text
    b"USERDATA",                # user data tag
    b"\r\n\r\n",              # header/body separator
]

# Predefined length cases to exercise corner sizes inside [1..1024]
INTERESTING_SIZES = [1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128,
                     255, 256, 257, 511, 512, 513, 768, 1000, 1023, 1024]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix of structured chunks and random bytes for diversity
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        choice = rng.randint(0, 4)
        remain = n - len(out)
        if choice == 0 and remain >= 4:
            # Insert a small structured header-like sequence
            tag = rng.choice(ASCII_MARKERS)
            out.extend(tag[:min(remain, len(tag))])
        elif choice == 1:
            # Repeated byte run
            b = rng.randrange(256)
            run = rng.randint(1, min(32, remain))
            out.extend(bytes([b]) * run)
        elif choice == 2 and remain >= 8:
            # Patterned increasing bytes
            start = rng.randrange(256)
            run = rng.randint(8, min(64, remain))
            out.extend(bytes((start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(run)))
        else:
            # Pure random
            chunk = os.urandom(min(remain, rng.randint(1, 64)))
            out.extend(chunk)
    return bytes(out[:n])


def _build_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose a target scenario: main buffer (<=1024) or user_data (<=64)
    scenario = rng.choice(["create_wrap", "user_data"])
    if scenario == "create_wrap":
        # Select a size within [1..1024], biased to interesting sizes
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            size = rng.choice(INTERESTING_SIZES)
        else:
            size = rng.randint(1, MAX_CREATE_WRAP)
    else:
        # user_data path
        interesting_user_sizes = [1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64]
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            size = rng.choice(interesting_user_sizes)
        else:
            size = rng.randint(1, MAX_USER_DATA)

    # Build content with markers at boundaries to exercise memcpy sizes
    body = _rand_bytes(rng, size)

    # Occasionally prefix or suffix with recognizable tokens, still within size bounds
    if size >= 8 and rng.random() < 0.5:
        tok = rng.choice(ASCII_MARKERS)
        # Place token at start or end by blending with body
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            body = (tok + body)[:size]
        else:
            body = (body + tok)[:size]

    return body


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Compose one or more payloads concatenated, but keep <= 4096 bytes.
    # The fuzzer harness typically consumes a single FUZZ_PARAM_STR per call,
    # but multiple stubs may be invoked; concatenating can give more variety.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0
    n_parts = rng.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(n_parts):
        p = _build_payload(rng)
        if total + len(p) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        parts.append(p)
        total += len(p)

    data = b"".join(parts)
    # Ensure non-empty and within bounds
    if not data:
        data = _build_payload(rng)
    return data[:MAX_TOTAL]

generators.data_type: AV1 bitstream (OBU sequence header or mixed OBUs)
generators.generator:
import random
from typing import List

# This generator produces a valid AV1 byte buffer containing OBUs, ensuring that
# at least one valid Sequence Header OBU is present (the last one), optionally
# surrounded by other benign OBUs. The OBU headers and leb128 sizes are encoded
# per AV1 spec. The sequence header payload is constructed to be consistent and
# simple, following the semantics described in the dav1d headers. It should be
# accepted by dav1d_parse_sequence_header() and yield a populated Dav1dSequenceHeader.

# Utility: leb128 unsigned integer encoding (8-bit groups, msb=1 for continuation)
def uleb128(n: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        b = n & 0x7F
        n >>= 7
        if n:
            out.append(0x80 | b)
        else:
            out.append(b)
            break
    return bytes(out)

# Bit writer helper to assemble bitfields
def bw_write_bits(val: int, nbits: int, acc_bits: List[int]):
    for i in range(nbits - 1, -1, -1):
        acc_bits.append((val >> i) & 1)

def bw_align_to_byte(acc_bits: List[int]):
    while len(acc_bits) % 8 != 0:
        acc_bits.append(0)

def bw_to_bytes(acc_bits: List[int]) -> bytes:
    bw_align_to_byte(acc_bits)
    out = bytearray()
    for i in range(0, len(acc_bits), 8):
        byte = 0
        for b in acc_bits[i:i+8]:
            byte = (byte << 1) | b
        out.append(byte)
    return bytes(out)

# Encode minimal timing_info (present flag separate outside) and operating points to keep parser happy
def build_sequence_header_bits(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    bits: List[int] = []

    # profile: choose based on layout/bits to remain consistent (0,1,2). We'll pick a consistent trio later.
    profile = rng.choice([0, 1])  # stick to common profiles
    bw_write_bits(profile, 3, bits)  # 3 bits in AV1 spec

    # still_picture / reduced_still_picture_header: keep both zero for general stream
    bw_write_bits(0, 1, bits)
    bw_write_bits(0, 1, bits)

    # timing_info_present_flag
    timing_info_present = rng.choice([0, 1])
    bw_write_bits(timing_info_present, 1, bits)
    if timing_info_present:
        # num_units_in_display_tick (32 bits)
        bw_write_bits(1000, 32, bits)
        # time_scale (32 bits)
        bw_write_bits(60000, 32, bits)
        # equal_picture_interval flag
        bw_write_bits(0, 1, bits)
        # decoder_model_info_present_flag
        bw_write_bits(0, 1, bits)
    # initial_display_delay_present_flag (when timing present). Keep 0 if present
    if timing_info_present:
        bw_write_bits(0, 1, bits)

    # operating_points_cnt_minus_1 (5 bits). choose 0 => 1 operating point
    bw_write_bits(0, 5, bits)
    # For each operating point (one): operating_point_idc (12 bits)
    bw_write_bits(0, 12, bits)
    # seq_level_idx (5 bits) choose level 10 (Main 3.1) or 13 etc; pick 10
    bw_write_bits(10, 5, bits)
    # seq_tier (1 bit) only if level not 31; write 0
    bw_write_bits(0, 1, bits)
    # decoder_model_present_for_this_op (1 bit) -> 0
    bw_write_bits(0, 1, bits)
    # initial_display_delay_present_for_this_op (1 bit) -> 0
    bw_write_bits(0, 1, bits)

    # frame_id_numbers_present_flag
    bw_write_bits(0, 1, bits)

    # seq_constraints
    # bit_depth: map to hbd later, but spec fields differ. We'll set twelve_bit=0, high_bitdepth flag optionally.
    high_bitdepth = rng.choice([0, 1])
    twelve_bit = 0
    monochrome = rng.choice([0, 1])
    chroma_subsampling_x = 0
    chroma_subsampling_y = 0
    # For profile 0: only 4:2:0 or mono at 8/10 bit; enforce subsampling 4:2:0 if not mono
    if profile == 0:
        if monochrome:
            chroma_subsampling_x = 0
            chroma_subsampling_y = 0
        else:
            chroma_subsampling_x = 1
            chroma_subsampling_y = 1
    elif profile == 1:
        # 4:4:4
        chroma_subsampling_x = 0
        chroma_subsampling_y = 0
    # Write constraint flags per spec ordering
    bw_write_bits(still_picture:=0, 1, bits)  # reserved till constraints in recent spec drafts; keep 0s
    bw_write_bits(reduced_still_picture_header:=0, 1, bits)
    bw_write_bits(twelve_bit, 1, bits)
    bw_write_bits(high_bitdepth, 1, bits)
    bw_write_bits(monochrome, 1, bits)
    bw_write_bits(chroma_subsampling_x, 1, bits)
    bw_write_bits(chroma_subsampling_y, 1, bits)
    # chroma_sample_position (2 bits) if subsampled; if not subsampled, write 0
    csp = 0
    if not monochrome and (chroma_subsampling_x or chroma_subsampling_y):
        csp = rng.choice([0, 1, 2])
    bw_write_bits(csp, 2, bits)
    # color_range bit (full/limited): 0 limited, 1 full
    color_range = rng.choice([0, 1])
    bw_write_bits(color_range, 1, bits)

    # subsampling_x/y additional reserved bits for profile 1+ at 12-bit not used here; pad zeros as per spec
    # film_grain_params_present: choose randomly
    film_grain_present = rng.choice([0, 1])
    bw_write_bits(film_grain_present, 1, bits)

    # color_config: color_description_present_flag
    color_description_present = rng.choice([0, 1])
    bw_write_bits(color_description_present, 1, bits)
    if color_description_present:
        # color_primaries (8 bits)
        bw_write_bits(rng.choice([1, 9, 13, 255]), 8, bits)
        # transfer_characteristics (8 bits)
        bw_write_bits(rng.choice([1, 13, 16, 18, 255]), 8, bits)
        # matrix_coefficients (8 bits)
        mc = rng.choice([0, 1, 6, 9, 14, 255])
        bw_write_bits(mc, 8, bits)
        # color_range already written earlier, but spec places it here; duplicate writing avoided by sticking to this path
    # separate_uv_delta_q flag
    bw_write_bits(rng.choice([0, 1]), 1, bits)

    # max_frame_width_minus_1 and height (16 bits each) choose common sizes
    max_w = rng.choice([640, 854, 1280, 1920, 2560, 3840])
    max_h = rng.choice([360, 480, 720, 1080, 1440, 2160])
    bw_write_bits(max_w - 1, 16, bits)
    bw_write_bits(max_h - 1, 16, bits)

    # order_hint_bits minus flags: enable order_hint and pick 7 bits commonly
    enable_order_hint = rng.choice([0, 1])
    bw_write_bits(enable_order_hint, 1, bits)
    if enable_order_hint:
        bw_write_bits(rng.choice([3, 5, 7]), 3, bits)  # order_hint_bits_minus_1 (3 bits representing 0..7)

    # enable_cdef, enable_restoration, enable_warped_motion etc. Keep a set of common flags
    bw_write_bits(1, 1, bits)  # enable_cdef
    bw_write_bits(1, 1, bits)  # enable_restoration
    bw_write_bits(1, 1, bits)  # enable_warped_motion
    bw_write_bits(1, 1, bits)  # enable_ref_frame_mvs

    # Reserved trailing bits not strictly needed; align
    return bw_to_bytes(bits)

# Build a generic non-critical metadata OBU (e.g., padding or metadata) to mix in
def build_simple_obu(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    obu_type = rng.choice([15, 5, 2])  # PADDING, METADATA, TEMPORAL_DELIMITER
    payload_len = rng.randint(0, 16)
    payload = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(payload_len))
    obu_header = build_obu_header(obu_type, obu_has_size_field=True, obu_extension_flag=False)
    return obu_header + uleb128(len(payload)) + payload

# Construct OBU header per AV1: forbidden(1)=0, type(4), ext(1), has_size_field(1), reserved(1)=0
def build_obu_header(obu_type: int, obu_has_size_field: bool, obu_extension_flag: bool) -> bytes:
    forbidden = 0
    extension = 1 if obu_extension_flag else 0
    has_size = 1 if obu_has_size_field else 0
    header = (forbidden << 7) | ((obu_type & 0x0F) << 3) | (extension << 2) | (has_size << 1) | 0
    out = bytearray([header])
    if extension:
        # temporal_id 3 bits, spatial_id 2 bits, reserved 3 bits
        out.append(0)  # simplest: all zeros
    return bytes(out)

# Sequence header OBU builder
def build_sequence_header_obu(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    sh_bytes = build_sequence_header_bits(rng)
    header = build_obu_header(1, obu_has_size_field=True, obu_extension_flag=False)  # type=SEQ_HDR
    return header + uleb128(len(sh_bytes)) + sh_bytes

# Public API
# Generate a bytes buffer containing a mix of OBUs with the last being a valid Sequence Header OBU.
def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    obus = []

    # Optionally prefix with a temporal delimiter and some padding/metadata
    prefix_count = rng.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(prefix_count):
        obus.append(build_simple_obu(rng))

    # Ensure at least one valid sequence header
    obus.append(build_sequence_header_obu(rng))

    # Optionally add additional OBUs before a final overriding sequence header (so the last SH is used)
    extra = rng.choice([0, 1])
    if extra:
        # some tiles/frames placeholders as padding/metadata
        mid_count = rng.randint(0, 2)
        for _ in range(mid_count):
            obus.append(build_simple_obu(rng))
        # Final sequence header to be the last one
        obus.append(build_sequence_header_obu(rng))

    buf = b"".join(obus)
    # Cap size to 4096 just in case (should be much smaller)
    return buf[:4096]
